q: 201. While procuring the consulting services, R.F.P. is extended to ..............
explain: In the procurement of consulting services, an Expression of Interest (EOI) is conducted first. The Request for Proposal (RFP) is then specifically issued only to those firms that have been shortlisted.

q: 202. Selected the incorrect statements ..............
options: a critical path always begins at the very first event
a critical path always terminates at the last event
critical activities control the project duration
critical activity is the one for which free float is zero
explain: A critical activity is defined by having a Total Float of zero. While its free float will also be zero, the primary defining characteristic used in network analysis is the zero total float.

q: 203. Quality assurance is achieved by ..............
explain: While the contractor is responsible for Quality Control (QC), Quality Assurance (QA) is the systematic process performed by the Engineer/Client to ensure that the quality requirements are being met.

q: 204. The constraints in case of resource smoothening operation would be ..............
options: both resources and project duration time
explain: In resource smoothening, the project duration is kept fixed (constrained), and resources are adjusted within the available floats to reduce peak demands.

q: 205. Updating may result in ..............
explain: Updating a project schedule based on actual progress can result in a new critical path, or an increase/decrease in the remaining project duration.

q: 206. Crash project duration is obtained by summing the ..............
options: normal durations for all the activities
crash durations for all the activities along the critical path obtained by taking into account the normal duration for the activities
crash durations for all the activities along the critical path obtained by taking into account the crash duration for all the activities
explain: The crash project duration is the shortest possible time to complete the project, calculated by summing the crash durations of activities along the path that remains critical when all activities are crashed.

options: time optimisation is given prime importance
cost optimisation is given prime importance
cost is directly proportional to time
explain: CPM is a deterministic model often used in construction where cost-time trade-offs (crashing) are a primary focus to find the optimum project cost.

q: 208. Indirect cost of the project ..............
options: decrease up to optimum duration and then increase with duration
explain: Indirect costs (overhead, administration, insurance) are time-dependent; the longer the project continues, the higher the total indirect cost.

q: 209. If a contractor is found corrupt for tender work, then what should be done by concerned office?
explain: Under standard procurement rules, if corruption is detected during the tender process, the immediate administrative action is the cancellation of that contractor's tender.

q: 210. The process of removal and loading of broken rock pieces from a tunnel is known as ..............
explain: Mucking is the specific term used in tunneling and mining for the removal of blasted or excavated rock (muck) from the working face.

q: 211. The effectiveness of explosion during increases by the process of ..............
explain: Stemming involves packing inert material (like clay or sand) into the drill hole above the explosive charge to confine the gases, significantly increasing the blast's effectiveness.

q: 212. Work study comprises ..............
explain: Work study is a generic term for those techniques, particularly method study and work measurement, which are used in the examination of human work.

q: 213. Gnatt chart indicates ..............
options: balance of work to be done
comparison of actual progress with the scheduled progress
explain: Gantt charts are primarily used for scheduling and monitoring, allowing managers to see actual progress bars plotted against the original planned bars.

q: 214. On a bar chart the various activities of a project are shown by ..............
explain: In a bar (Gantt) chart, the time dimension is on the horizontal axis, so activities are represented by horizontal bars or lines representing their duration.

q: 215. Jobs going ahead of schedule are conveniently shown in ..............
explain: The Gantt chart is the most effective tool for visualizing schedule variance (ahead or behind) by comparing current progress against the baseline.

q: 216. The weakness in bar chart is ..............
options: uncertainty in duration for various activities
the sequence of activities is not very clear
explain: Bar charts struggle to show complex interdependencies between activities, do not account for uncertainty well, and can become cluttered for large projects.

q: 217. A milestone chart ..............
options: shows the interdependence of various jobs
shows the events in chronological, but not in a logical sequence
explain: A milestone chart is an improvement over the bar chart that identifies key events (milestones) chronologically, though it still lacks the detailed logical network of CPM.

q: 218. The interrelationship between the functional elements of a programme is achieve through ..............
explain: A Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) hierarchically organizes the project into functional elements, showing how sub-tasks relate to the overall project scope.

options: a definite position of an activity
explain: In network analysis, an event (node) represents a specific point in time—the start or completion of an activity—and does not consume time or resources.

q: 220. The scheduled completion time of an operation in C.P.M. chart is mentioned on ..............
options: left top corner outside the circle
left top corner inside the circle
explain: In standard network notation (AOA), the Earliest Start Time (EST) or scheduled time is often noted in the top-left quadrant outside the event circle.

q: 221. The probability factor Z in P.E.R.T. is given by ..............
options: scheduled time - earliest expected time / standard deviation
scheduled time - latest allowable time / variance
latest allowable time - scheduled time / standard deviation
explain: The Z-score formula in PERT is (Ts - Te) / S, where Ts is the target/scheduled time and Te is the expected completion time.

q: 222. If the probability factor is zero, the chances of completing the project in scheduled time are ..............
explain: A Z-score of 0 indicates that the scheduled time is equal to the expected time. In a normal distribution, this represents the 50th percentile (50% probability).

q: 223. Float may be defined as the difference between ..............
options: latest start time and the earliest start time
latest finish time and the earliest finish time
time available and the time required to complete the activity
explain: Total Float can be calculated as LST-EST or LFT-EFT, and it essentially represents the excess time available for an activity.

q: 224. Which of the following is a P.E.R.T. event?
explain: Events are instantaneous points in time. 'Concreting of roof completed' signifies the end of an activity, whereas the other options describe ongoing activities.

q: 225. Of the following the P.E.R.T. event is ..............
explain: In PERT, an event represents the accomplishment of a task at a specific point in time. 'Concrete cured' indicates a finished state/event.

q: 226. In P.E.R.T. analysis the actual performance of task is known is ..............
explain: In PERT (Program Evaluation and Review Technique), the focus is on the completion of tasks, which are represented as 'events' or milestones in the network.

q: 227. In P.E.R.T. analysis, the start and end of event is represented by ..............
explain: In a PERT network, the nodes represent events, marking the start or the finish of one or more activities.

q: 228. Which of the following in an activity ..............
explain: An activity consumes time and resources. 'Excavation' is a continuous process/task, whereas 'cured' or 'plastered' (in past tense) usually denotes an event or state.

q: 229. An activity requires ..............
explain: By definition, an activity in project management is a specific task that consumes both time (duration) and resources (labor, money, materials).

q: 230. A drawback of the bar chart is that ..............
options: it is difficult to judge whether an activity is completed or not
all the activities represented are independent of each other
sequence of activities is not clearly defined
it is not possible to judge whether the activity is ahead or behind schedule
explain: The primary limitation of a Gantt/Bar chart is its inability to show the complex logical interdependencies and sequences between different activities.

q: 231. Milestones are ..............
options: the events specifying the beginning and /or the end of subdivided activities
the stones indicating the distance along a highway
dates of important happenings in the history of any nation
explain: In project management, milestones are key events that represent significant points of progress, such as the start or completion of a major phase.

q: 232. Henry Gantt developed the bar chart technique around ..............
explain: Henry Gantt developed his famous chart around the year 1910 (early 1900s) to help supervisors see whether production was on schedule.

q: 233. Milestone charts are developed around ..............
explain: Milestone charts were developed as an evolution of the bar chart, gaining prominence around the 1940s during World War II industrial efforts.

q: 234. The earliest method used for planning of projects was ..............
explain: The Bar Chart (Gantt Chart) is the oldest formal technique for project planning, predating the network techniques like PERT and CPM which arrived in the 1950s.

q: 235. Bar charts are suitable only for ..............
explain: Due to their inability to show interdependencies, bar charts become too complex and confusing for major projects, making them best suited for simple or minor projects.

q: 236. P.E.R.T. is an abbreviation for ..............
options: pertinent equation related to a task
explain: PERT stands for Program (or Project) Evaluation and Review Technique, originally developed by the US Navy.

q: 237. Expected project duration generally follows ..............
explain: While individual activity durations in PERT follow a Beta distribution, the Central Limit Theorem states that the total project duration (sum of activities) follows a Normal distribution.

q: 238. The area under the β-distribution curve is divided into two equal parts by ..............
explain: The 'expected time' ($t_e$) is the weighted average (mean) which theoretically divides the probability distribution into two equal areas of probability.

q: 239. Which of the following does not represent an activity?
options: the office area is being cleaned
explain: 'Site located' is an event (a milestone or result), whereas the other three options describe ongoing processes that consume time and effort.

q: 240. The most suitable type of equipment for compaction of cohesive soils is ..............
explain: Sheep foot rollers are designed to provide high pressure and 'kneading' action, which is essential for compacting cohesive (clayey) soils.
CPM stands for Critical Path Method, a deterministic algorithm for scheduling a set of project activities.
PERT focuses on milestones and the reaching of specific events, making it an 'event-oriented' technique compared to CPM's activity focus.
CPM focuses on the duration and sequence of tasks themselves, classifying it as an 'activity-oriented' network technique.
Because PERT uses three time estimates (optimistic, pessimistic, most likely) to account for uncertainty, it is considered a probabilistic approach.

q: 245. The authority of variation order up to 25% of contract cost lies on ..............
explain: In accordance with Nepalese Public Procurement regulations, the Department Head (Chief) generally has the delegated authority to approve variations up to a certain percentage (25%).

q: 246. The authority of variation order above 25% of contract cost lies on ..............
explain: Major variations exceeding standard departmental limits (typically above 25%) require higher-level approval from the Council of Ministers (Cabinet).
CPM assumes that activity durations are known with certainty, hence it uses a single time estimate and is called a deterministic approach.

q: 248. Which of the following statements is true?
options: P.E.R.T. is activity oriented and adopts deterministic approach
C.P.M. is event oriented and adopts probabilistic approach
C.P.M. is activity oriented and adopts probabilistic approach
P.E.R.T. is event oriented and adopts probabilistic approach
explain: This statement correctly combines the two fundamental characteristics of PERT: it is event-based and handles uncertainty using probability.

q: 249. When the events are numbered in a network then the number of the head event of an activity is ..............
options: always larger than the number of the tail event of same activity
always smaller than the number of the tail event of the same activity
always equal to the number of the tail event of the same activity
explain: Following Fulkerson's Rule for numbering networks, the head node (j) must always be assigned a number greater than the tail node (i).

q: 250. The time corresponding to minimum total project cost is ..............
options: between normal time and crash time
explain: The 'Optimum Duration' occurs where the sum of direct and indirect costs is at its minimum, which usually falls between the crash duration and the normal duration.

q: 251. The cost slope is defined as ..............
options: (normal cost - crash cost) / (normal time - crash time)
(crash cost - normal cost) / (normal time - crash time)
explain: Cost slope represents the increase in cost per unit of time saved. It is calculated as the change in cost divided by the change in time: (Crash Cost - Normal Cost) / (Normal Time - Crash Time).

q: 252. While bid evaluation, if unit rate and total amount are contradicted, then which of the following will prevail ..............
options: unit price is adopted and total amount is corrected
explain: Standard procurement guidelines (including PPMO) state that the unit price quoted in words or figures prevails. If the total is wrong due to a calculation error, the unit rate is used to correct the total.

q: 253. In Q.C.B.S. method of procurement, evaluation of consulting firms to award the contract, the weightage will be ..............
explain: Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) typically gives high priority to technical competence. A common standard weightage is 80% for the technical proposal and 20% for the financial proposal.

q: 254. Earliest finish of an activity is always ..............
options: greater than earliest event time of the following node
less than earliest event time of the following node
less than or equal to earliest event time of the following node
greater than or equal to earliest event time of the following node
explain: The earliest event time ($T_E$) of a node is the maximum of the earliest finish times ($EF$) of all activities merging into that node. Therefore, any individual $EF$ must be $\le$ the node's $T_E$.

q: 255. Select the incorrect statement
options: earliest start of an activity is the early event time of the node it leaves
latest finish of an activity is the late event time of the node it enters
latest start of an activity is its latest finish minus its duration
explain: All the statements (a), (b), and (c) are standard definitions in CPM/PERT. Since none are incorrect, the answer is 'none of the above'.

q: 256. If the optimistic time, most likely time and pessimistic time for activity A are 4, 6 and 8 respectively and for activity B are 5, 5.5 and 9 respectively, then ............
options: expected time of activity A is greater than the expected time of activity B
expected time of activity B is greater than the expected time of activity A
expected time of both activities A and B are same
explain: Expected time $t_e = (t_o + 4t_m + t_p) / 6$. For A: $(4+24+8)/6 = 6$. For B: $(5+22+9)/6 = 6$. Both are equal.

q: 257. If an activity has its optimistic, most likely and pessimistic times as 2, 3 and 7 respectively, than its expected time and variance are respectively ............
258. Select the incorrect statement ............
options: start float and finish float are always equal
total float can be either start float or finish float
start float and finish float need not be equal
start float and finish float are the differences between activity times and not event times
explain: Start float and finish float are equal to each other (and to Total Float) only if the activity is not part of a sub-network with interference. They are not 'always' equal in general context.

q: 259. For a given size of bucket, the ideal output of a dragline will be least in ............
explain: Wet sticky clay has high adhesion and cohesion, making it difficult to dump from the bucket and slow to cut, leading to the lowest output.

q: 260. Which one of the following surface will give highest coefficient of traction while using crawler track tractors?
explain: Concrete provides a hard, high-friction surface that allows the tracks to grip efficiently without slipping, unlike loose sand or ice.

q: 261. Which of the following surfaces will give highest rolling resistance for a rubber tyred vehicle?
explain: Loose sand deforms significantly under rubber tires, consuming energy and creating the highest resistance to movement.

q: 262. The probability of completion of any activity within its expected time is ............
explain: In PERT, the expected time ($t_e$) corresponds to the mean of a normal distribution (50% probability).

q: 263. Functional organization system of working was introduced by ............
explain: Frederick Winslow Taylor, the father of scientific management, introduced functional foremanship/organization.

q: 264. In resources levelling ............
options: total duration of project is increased
uniform demand of resources is achieved
explain: Resource leveling aims to smooth out the resource usage profile to achieve a more uniform demand throughout the project.

q: 265. Total cost of the project is ............
options: direct cost and outage loss of project
explain: The total project cost is the summation of Direct Costs (labor, material) and Indirect Costs (overhead, insurance).

q: 266. In time-cost optimisation of a project, crashing is done ............
options: on all the activities lying on the critical paths
only on activities lying on the original critical path and having flatter cost slopes
on original critical activities and those that become critical
explain: Crashing must be performed on critical activities to reduce project duration; as paths change, new critical activities must also be crashed.

q: 267. Site order book is used for recoding ............
options: indents for materials to be ordered
explain: The site order book is maintained at the site to record instructions given by supervising officers (like the Executive Engineer).

q: 268. The problem of developing, low cost housing for economically backward people in undeveloped region should be analysed by ............
explain: PERT is used for research and development type projects where time estimates are uncertain and non-repetitive.

q: 269. In P.E.R.T. technique the critical path has slack equal to ............
explain: Critical path events have the minimum slack, which can be zero (on schedule) or negative (behind schedule).

q: 270. Bid bond is ............% of quoted amount.
explain: Commonly, Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) or Bid Bonds range from 1% to 2.5% of the estimated cost.

q: 271. Contractor is liable to maintain the defects upto ............
explain: The Defect Liability Period (DLP) is the timeframe during which the contractor is responsible for repairing any faults.

q: 272. Direct purchase can be done for procurement of consulting services or construction works upto ............
options: 5 lakh in case of consulting services
5 lakh in case of construction works
explain: Specific financial thresholds for direct purchase vary by regional governing rules, but 5 lakh is generally not the standard limit for both simultaneously.

q: 273. The C.P.M. network is updated ............
options: whenever the is difference in the planned and actual performance
explain: Updating is necessary whenever there is a significant deviation between planned progress and actual field performance.

q: 274. The effect of network compression is increase in the ............
explain: Compressing (crashing) a network involves adding more resources, which directly increases the direct cost.

q: 275. The scheduling of project activities is done in such a way that it consumes resources ............
options: greater at the start, lesser at the end
lesser at the start, greater at the end
explain: Ideal resource scheduling aims for a uniform distribution to avoid idle time and sudden spikes in labor/equipment needs.

q: 276. The process of inspiring the subordinates to do work or achieve an objective is called as ............
explain: Motivation is the psychological process that encourages workers to give their best to reach a goal.

q: 277. In a barchart the vertical axis represents ............
explain: In a standard Gantt/Bar chart, the Y-axis lists the activities, while the X-axis represents time.

q: 278. The barchart technique is commonly used because it ............
options: is simple to draw and easy to understand
is useful for cost and quality control
explain: The primary advantage of bar charts is their simplicity and visual clarity for general project overviews.

q: 279. The main function of the construction management is ............
explain: Management involves planning, organizing, staffing, directing, and controlling (POSDCORB).

q: 280. Each work should be planned with respect to ............
options: manner of execution of the work
explain: Effective planning requires considering the methods (how), timing (urgency), and necessary inputs (resources).

q: 281. In construction work, the controlling function aims at ............
options: keeping a watch over the physical progress of each activity of the work
controlling the expenditure on each item of work
controlling the use of machines and materials
explain: Controlling ensures that physical progress, financial expenditure, and resource usage stay within the project budget and schedule.

q: 282. Which of the following is an example of parallel activities?
options: construction of walls and casting of roof
construction of walls and carpentry work of doors and window
casting of roof and construction of septic tank
digging of well and construction of septic tank
explain: Carpentry work for doors/windows can happen simultaneously (in parallel) while walls are being built.

q: 283. The occurrence of the completion of an activity is called its ............
explain: In an activity-on-arrow diagram, the head of the arrow signifies the completion event.

q: 284. The occurrence of the starting of an activity is called its ............
explain: The tail of the arrow represents the start event of that specific activity.

q: 285. In a functional organization ............
options: specialised knowledge and guidance to individual worker is provided
explain: Functional organizations allow for specialization, leading to better quality, less waste, and expert supervision.

q: 286. The salient feature of the organization evolved by F.W. Taylor is ............
options: separation of planning and design part for field work
explain: Taylorism emphasizes scientific methods, specialization, and separating planning from manual execution.

q: 287. The major principle of an organization is ..............
explain: Duplicate of 281. Key management principles used to structure efficient workflows and accountability.

q: 288. Time and progress chart are also known as ..............
explain: Duplicate of 282. Reflects the various ways to visualize the timeline and status of a project.

q: 289. The process of calculating the resources requirement of a project is known as ..............
explain: Resource aggregation is the summation of resources required across all activities for each time period.

q: 290. The use of bar chart is very popular in construction department because ..............
options: it is very simple to prepare and interpret
each item of work or activity is shown separately
modification to the chart, if required, can be carried out easily
explain: Duplicate of 284 with expanded answer. Its simplicity and clarity make it widely used despite its technical limitations.

q: 291. Military type of organization is known as ..............
explain: Duplicate of 285. In a line organization, there is a clear, direct vertical relationship between different levels of management.

q: 292. In the L.I.B. type of contract management, the acronym stands for ..............
explain: Wait, correcting from earlier: In the context of international procurement, LIB often refers to Limited International Bidding, which is used when there are only a limited number of suppliers.

q: 293. The pre qualification criteria is approved by ..............
explain: In standard government procurement in Nepal, major tender criteria (like pre-qualification) are officially approved by the Department Head (Director General).

q: 294. Which of the document is prepared and submitted by contractor?
explain: The contractor must submit a Quality Assurance Plan (QAP) to show how they intend to meet the project's quality requirements.

q: 295. Any delay in starting, that involves consumption of any of the interfering floats of an activity, will result in ..............
explain: Interfering float is the part of total float that consumes the slack of a succeeding activity. Using it will affect following activities but not necessarily the overall project duration (unless total float is exceeded).

q: 296. Which of the following earth moving machines has the shortest cycle time?
explain: A dipper shovel (power shovel) generally has the most efficient mechanical cycle and the highest digging force, leading to the shortest cycle time for heavy excavation.

q: 297. For which of the following materials, the output of power shovels for a fixed shovel size will be maximum ..............
explain: Moist loam is the ideal material for power shovels because it is easy to cut and fills the bucket efficiently without sticking or requiring excessive force.

q: 298. Which of the following excavators is most suitable for digging under water?
explain: Draglines have a long reach and use a cable-suspended bucket, making them the most effective choice for deep underwater excavation or dredging.

q: 299. The authority to conduct the monitoring of public procurement in Nepal lies with ..............
explain: The Public Procurement Monitoring Office (PPMO) is the central government body responsible for overseeing and monitoring procurement activities in Nepal.

q: 300. For the I.C.B. procurement method, the period of bidding to contractor must be at least ..............
explain: For International Competitive Bidding (ICB), standard regulations require a minimum bidding period of 45 days to allow international firms sufficient time to prepare proposals.
